what_it_does: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) are AI models for graphs that change over time — where new relationships appear, old ones vanish, and node features evolve. The challenge with accelerating them is that the graph's topology forces strict ordering: data from one time step must fully complete before the next can start, leaving most of the GPU idle and causing memory bottlenecks from unpredictable accesses to node features across the graph. TaGNN solves this by computing final results for some vertices in parallel while loading the features for unaffected vertices only once instead of repeatedly. The hardware memory is organized to group vertices by their topology and timestamps, making fetches more predictable. An additional optimization called similarity-aware cell skipping notices when certain calculations would produce nearly the same output as before and simply skips them, saving computation.
